You are a programming expert. 
        You will be provided with a patch used to fix a bug. 
        Based on the commit message and modifications in the patch, you need to analyze the root cause of the bug in detail. 

        Here is the patch content:
        From 38b1dc47a35ba14c3f4472138ea56d014c2d609b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2020 14:04:51 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] rxrpc: Fix server keyring leak

If someone calls setsockopt() twice to set a server key keyring, the first
keyring is leaked.

Fix it to return an error instead if the server key keyring is already set.

Fixes: 17926a79320a ("[AF_RXRPC]: Provide secure RxRPC sockets for use by userspace and kernel both")
Signed-off-by: David Howells <dhowells@redhat.com>
---
 net/rxrpc/key.c | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/net/rxrpc/key.c b/net/rxrpc/key.c
index 75e84ed4fa63..2e8bd3b97301 100644
--- a/net/rxrpc/key.c
+++ b/net/rxrpc/key.c
@@ -903,7 +903,7 @@ int rxrpc_request_key(struct rxrpc_sock *rx, sockptr_t optval, int optlen)
 
 	_enter("");
 
-	if (optlen <= 0 || optlen > PAGE_SIZE - 1)
+	if (optlen <= 0 || optlen > PAGE_SIZE - 1 || rx->securities)
 		return -EINVAL;
 
 	description = memdup_sockptr_nul(optval, optlen);
-- 
2.25.1


        
        Provide a response strictly in the following format:
        Root cause:<Root cause>

Root cause: The bug was caused by the lack of a check to prevent the setting of a server key keyring if one was already set. This led to a memory leak when `setsockopt()` was called multiple times to set the server key keyring, as the first keyring was not properly released before the second one was assigned. The patch adds a condition to return an error if the server key keyring is already set, thus preventing the leak.
